category: Operational ontology inside a data platform
licence_pricing: Proprietary; no public list price found (palantir.com/pricing redirects to corporate homepage); enterprise contract only
deployment: Palantir-hosted Foundry; Apollo referenced in docs nav for deployment; self-hosted/air-gapped terms not verified
inputs: Foundry datasets and streams; object types, link types, interfaces, value types, action types
entry_criteria: Foundry contract; data already in Foundry; Ontology Manager UI or @osdk/maker TypeScript build pipeline
how_layer_built: Human modeller: object types with primary key, links by FK or intermediary object, interfaces with implementations, value types with constraints, actions, derived properties across multi-hop links; or code-first @osdk/maker
automation_level: Low for modelling; high for app/SDK generation from the model
human_in_loop: Strong: ontology branching and proposals; interface schema migrations with 7-180 day grace period and schema lockfile; build-time compatibility checks
artifacts_exit_criteria: Ontology (object/link/action/interface/value types), generated OSDK packages, apps, AIP agents, branch proposals
time_versioning: Value-type versions; interface schema migrations time-boxed and enforced; ontology branching; no documented valid-from/valid-to on links
lineage_provenance: Foundry dataset lineage exists; ontology-level provenance not documented in fetched pages
agent_consumption: OSDK typed SDKs, platform APIs, AIP, ontology-augmented generation page in docs nav
problems_solved: Operational apps, decision support, digital twins, permission-aware workflows
documented_outcomes: Vendor customer stories and investor materials; not independently verified
limits: Enterprise cost and lock-in; requires Foundry data estate; modelling skill; no documented uncertainty/confidence labels
gap_for_us: Highest bar and strongest semantics, but only inside Foundry; our opening is the same typed object/link/action model auto-derived, local and provenance-labelled
notes: Pricing: do not quote a number. Docs body is JS-rendered; only navigation retrieved. Value-type versions and interface migrations verified in OSDK Maker README.

category: Governance and metadata catalog plus semantic layer inside lakehouse
licence_pricing: No standalone Unity Catalog list price found; billed via Databricks compute (DBUs); Data Classification is its own billing SKU at list prices from system.billing.list_prices
deployment: Databricks managed service on AWS/Azure/GCP; open-source Unity Catalog implementation also published
inputs: Tables, views, volumes, functions, models, services in a UC metastore; managed tables must be Delta or Iceberg; external assets registered as external metadata
entry_criteria: Databricks workspace with UC metastore; Databricks Runtime 11.3 LTS+; standard or dedicated access mode; account-level groups
how_layer_built: Metadata-driven: automatic table and column lineage from queries/jobs/notebooks/dashboards; LLM agent auto-classification and tagging; metric views authored in SQL DDL or UI with YAML validation and agent metadata (synonyms, display names)
automation_level: High for technical metadata; low for business meaning; no class/relation ontology
human_in_loop: Classification review and exclusion (removes tag, suppresses re-tagging, feeds accuracy); metric view lifecycle; permissions
artifacts_exit_criteria: Governed catalog, tags, table+column lineage graph, metric views queryable from SQL/BI/Genie/alerts, system tables for lineage and classification
time_versioning: Lineage UI back to 2024-09-01 with all-time option; system tables rolling 1 year; not preserved across renames; no documented bitemporal edges
lineage_provenance: Best-in-class SQL lineage (table/column, jobs, dashboards, models, external assets) with permission masking; not fact-level provenance
agent_consumption: Genie Code lineage Q&A; Genie Agents query metric views; MCP services governed as securables
problems_solved: Governance, PII discovery and GDPR, impact analysis, root-cause tracing, metric consistency
limits: Databricks-only; external assets metadata-only; no entity identity/ontology; no reasoning; metric views are measures, not objects; lineage gaps for RDDs, path refs, UDF column lineage
gap_for_us: UC is the benchmark for automatic metadata capture; we can do the same for meaning (classes, keys, relations, time) on sources UC cannot see
notes: Doc updates: UC 2026-09-11, lineage 2026-10-26, metric views 2026-09-11, classification 2026-10-09, requirements 2026-09-16.

entry_criteria: Broad multi-tool data estate plus governance function; admins and stewards; budget in the $120K+ range
how_layer_built: Metadata-driven ingestion plus human curation plus Context Agents that draft tacit knowledge; Enterprise Data Graph across systems; Context Engineering Studio and Context Lakehouse (Iceberg-native, graph+file, vector-native)
automation_level: Medium: connectors and AI agents automate metadata capture; meaning still human-approved
human_in_loop: Central: stewards curate glossary/owners; AI agents draft context for approval
artifacts_exit_criteria: Catalog assets, glossary, lineage, ownership, quality/README context, context served to AI tools
time_versioning: Metadata history/versioning; decision history claimed; no bitemporal instance facts

category: Enterprise knowledge graph platform: OWL + inference + virtualization + NL
licence_pricing: Stardog Free: not open source, renewable 1-year licence, commercial use allowed, excludes HA, caching, backups, LDAP and full connector breadth. Enterprise: quote-only
deployment: On-prem, Stardog Cloud, AWS/Azure marketplaces, Docker/Kubernetes
inputs: RDBMS and NoSQL through virtual graphs (customer supplies JDBC drivers), CSV/JSON, RDF
entry_criteria: OWL/RDF modelling skills; JDBC connectivity; Enterprise licence for production
how_layer_built: Model-first OWL ontology plus mappings in SMS, R2RML or SMS2; mapping optional for RDBMS via R2RML direct mapping; inference rules extend model; virtual graphs query in place, virtual import materializes
automation_level: Low: mapping files are human-authored; direct mapping is table-level only
human_in_loop: Human designs ontology, mappings and rules; ICV constraints and reasoning explanations help debugging
artifacts_exit_criteria: Knowledge graph, registered virtual graphs, materialized copies, inference closure, SPARQL/GraphQL/SQL/BI/REST access, Voicebox
time_versioning: Point-in-time recovery tutorial; transaction logs; named graphs for versioning (D); no documented bitemporal edges
lineage_provenance: Reasoning explanation/debugging and inference provenance; inference provenance, not source-confidence provenance
agent_consumption: Voicebox NL Q&A; GraphQL; SQL/BI server; REST
problems_solved: Data fabric without copying, analytics modernization, drug discovery, operational risk, supply chain
documented_outcomes: Vendor customer stories; not independently verified
limits: SPARQL/OWL skills scarcity; documented SPARQL-to-SQL gaps (duplicate solutions, MINUS untranslated, datatype semantics, R2RML named graphs); mapping maintenance; no free HA; connectors paywalled
gap_for_us: Validates query-in-place; weakness is human authoring of ontology and mappings. We auto-derive a first model and let humans review
notes: Virtual graph details from https://docs.stardog.com/virtual-graphs/. Stardog Free is commercial, not open source.

vendor: Ontotext AD, doing business as Graphwise
category: RDF store with forward-chaining OWL reasoning and relational virtualization
licence_pricing: GraphDB Free: commercial and free, limited to 2 concurrent queries. Enterprise licensed per server CPU core, each node separately, roughly 1 concurrent query per core; per-core price not published. Standard Edition discontinued but supported
deployment: Java anywhere; Docker/Helm; AWS/Azure/GCP deployment guides; Raft HA cluster; multi-region
inputs: RDF; relational sources via data virtualization; Kafka/Solr/Elasticsearch/OpenSearch connectors in EE; FedX federation
entry_criteria: RDF/OWL skills; repository configuration and ruleset choice; licence planning by CPU core
how_layer_built: Model-first: import OWL/RDFS ontologies, choose ruleset (empty, rdfs, rdfsplus, owl-horst, owl-max, owl2-ql, owl2-rl; default RDFS-Plus); rules compiled to Java bytecode and total-materialized at load; custom rulesets in .pie; consistency checks available but off by default
automation_level: Inference automatic once configured; nothing auto-modelled from data
human_in_loop: Ontology and ruleset authoring; optional consistency-check policy; schema update transactions for offline schema change
artifacts_exit_criteria: Repository with explicit and inferred triples, fast SPARQL endpoint, explain plans, consistency reports, provenance plugin for inference closure by named graph
time_versioning: Named graphs, backup/restore, reinfer after ruleset change, schema transactions; no bitemporal edge model (D)
lineage_provenance: Provenance plugin regenerates inference closure from a named graph; inference provenance documented; not dataset lineage
agent_consumption: SPARQL/GraphQL/REST; Graphwise/metaphactory stack adds NL Q&A and agentic use cases
problems_solved: Semantic search, knowledge discovery, regulated industries, pharma/life-sciences ontologies, data federation
documented_outcomes: metaphactory case studies (Boehringer Ingelheim, Scania/TRATON, Sloane Lab) and metrics (BKW <2yr break-even, Siemens Energy 1500 hrs saved); vendor-reported
limits: Semantic skills; load-time materialization cost; schema-change friction; per-core licensing punishes concurrency; no auto-discovery; free tier effectively single-user
gap_for_us: Reasoning right, delivery enterprise-only; a lightweight local inference/validation layer with OWL/SHACL export is credible for mid-market
notes: Reasoning/ruleset details from https://graphdb.ontotext.com/documentation/10.8/reasoning.html. Docs footer: ONTOTEXT AD doing business as Graphwise.

category: Standards and free ontology editor, not a commercial layer
licence_pricing: Protege: free and open source. OWL 2: W3C Recommendation 2012-12-11. SHACL: W3C Recommendation 2017-07-20
deployment: Desktop and WebProtege; standards are runtime-agnostic
inputs: OWL ontologies, RDF graphs, SHACL shapes graphs
how_layer_built: Manual ontology engineering; SHACL shapes provide validation constraints and machine-readable validation reports (focus node, path, value, severity, message)
automation_level: None for data ingestion; reasoners can check consistency (not assessed here)
human_in_loop: Ontology engineer authors model and shapes
artifacts_exit_criteria: OWL file (classes, properties, individuals, profiles EL/QL/RL) and SHACL validation report
time_versioning: Ontology version IRIs (standard practice); file-based, no runtime history
lineage_provenance: No data lineage; SHACL report is constraint-level evidence
agent_consumption: None: no runtime, connectors or agent path
problems_solved: Interoperability, validation, regulated-industry vocabulary governance; used for OBO Foundry, WHO ICD-11, NCI Thesaurus
documented_outcomes: Adoption evidence via named projects on Protege site (vendor/academic)
limits: No connectors, no instance graph runtime, no lineage, no agent access; editor not a layer
gap_for_us: These are our interoperability contracts: export OWL/SHACL-compatible shapes so buyers are not locked in, and use SHACL-style validation reports as auditable evidence
